text:
Dubai residential activity accelerated over the last four weeks through 17 November 2026. The Land Department registered 13,702 sales totaling AED 39.47 billion, representing a 24.1 percent increase in volume and a 23.0 percent rise in value compared to the previous four weeks. Mortgage registrations were recorded separately at 5,505 transactions during the same period.

Median residential pricing reached AED 1,727 per square foot, up 3.4 percent from the prior period. Off-plan transactions accounted for 56.7 percent of total sales. In the rental market, 107,548 Ejari contracts were registered with a 51.9 percent renewal share. The median residential rent stood at AED 68,000 per annum.

Momentum varied significantly across communities. Al Yufrah 1 showed the strongest price appreciation at 36.4 percent over twelve weeks, followed by Dubai Industrial City at 9.3 percent and Dubai Production City at 8.1 percent. Conversely, Saih Shuaib 1 saw prices fall 29.5 percent, while Jumeirah Lakes Towers declined 16.6 percent. International City Phase 1 offered the highest estimated gross yield at 8.6 percent for flats, with Zaabeel First following at 8.4 percent.

Investors should monitor the 926 sales flagged as anomalies in the last 60 days, which deviated more than 35 percent from comparable medians. These figures are derived from registered DLD data and Ejari contracts. Medians are calculated after excluding bulk deals, partial-share transfers, portfolio blocks, mortgages, gifts, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
